en: The Primordial Hymn of Praise.
Oṃ, salutations to the Primordial One!
Listen, my child, I shall proclaim the hymn to the Primordial One, which yields great fruit;
he who recites it constantly with devotion is indeed beloved by Viṣṇu. (1)
In the Kali age, he has no fear whatsoever of death or disease;
even a childless woman obtains a son if she listens for three fortnights.
If one hears [this] from the mouth of a Brahmin for two months, there is liberation from bondage;
if one is a woman whose children have died, she shall have living children if she listens for six months.
In a ship, in distress, or in battle, one shall obtain victory through recitation;
having written it down and placed it in the home, there shall never be fear of fire or thieves.
In Rājasthāna she is eternally victorious, and all the deities are well-pleased with her.
Oṃ Hrīṃ! She is Brahmāṇī in the world of Brahmā, and Sarvamaṅgalā in Vaikuṇṭha. || 5 ||
Indrāṇī in Amarāvatī, Avikā in the abode of Varuṇa, Kālarūpā in the abode of Yama, and Śubhā in the palace of Kubera. || 6 ||
Mahānandā is in the southeast corner, Mṛgavāhinī in the northwest,
Raktadantā in the southwest, and Śūladhāriṇī in the northeast.
In Pātāla she is in the form of Vaiṣṇavī; in Siṃhala she is Devamohinī; in Maṇidvīpa she is Surasā; and in Laṅkā she is Bhadrakālikā.
Rāmeśvarī is at Setubandha, Vimalā at Puruṣottama,
Virajā in the land of Oḍra, and Kāmākṣī on the Nīla mountain.
Kālikā is in the land of Vaṅga, Maheśvarī is in Ayodhyā, Annapūrṇā is in Vārāṇasī, and Gayeśvarī is in the sacred field of Gayā. || 10 ||
In Kurukṣetra she is Bhadrakālī; in Vraja she is the supreme Kātyāyanī;
in Dvārakā she is Mahāmāyā; and in Mathurā she is Māheśvarī. (11)
You are the hunger of all beings, and you are the tide of the ocean;
you are the ninth day of the bright fortnight and the supreme eleventh day of the dark fortnight.
You are the goddess, the daughter of Dakṣa, the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice;
you are indeed Jānakī, the wife of Rāma, the one who brought about the destruction of Rāvaṇa. 13.
The Goddess who slew Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the destroyer of Raktabīja, the crusher of Niśumbha and Śumbha, and the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha. || 14 ||
Durgā bestows devotion to Viṣṇu and always grants happiness and liberation;
that man who constantly recites this meritorious primordial hymn [shall attain these]. (15)
There shall be no fear of any fever, and all diseases will be destroyed; he obtains the merit of ten million holy sites—of this there is no doubt. (16)
May Jayā protect me from the front, and Vijayā protect me from behind; may Nārāyaṇī protect the region of my head, and Siṃhavāhinī protect all my limbs.
Śivadūtī, Ugracaṇḍā, Pratyaṅgā, Parameśvarī, Viśālākṣī, Mahāmāyā, Kaumārī, Saṅkhinī, and Śivā. (18)
Cakriṇī, Jayadhātrī, Raṇamattā, Raṇapriyā, Durgā, Jayantī, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, and Mahodarī. || 19 ||
She is Nārasiṃhī and Vārāhī, the bestower of success and the giver of happiness;
she is terrifying and most fierce, the destroyer of great fear.
Thus ends the "Hymn to the Primordial Goddess" from the *Brahmayāmala*, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada.
Oṃ, salutations to the Primordial Goddess; Oṃ, salutations to the Primordial Goddess; Oṃ, salutations to the Primordial Goddess.
